items.title: Greek wildfire kills two people as aircraft deployed to blaze at Belgian nature reserve
items.summary_raw:

Two people have died in fires on the Greek island of Salamis as firefighting aircraft were called on to help tame the biggest blaze in Belgium in more than a century in the latest wave of European wildfires.

The bodies of two people were recovered from the Peristeria beach area of Salamis on Sunday after two fires broke out on the island, a fire department spokesperson told Agence France-Presse. Hundreds of people have been ordered to evacuate.

items.title: Andy Burnham has barely acknowledged the climate crisis. If only Britain’s workers had that luxury | John Harris
items.summary_raw:
Nurses collapsing, builders with heatstroke, bus drivers in cabs that reach 44C. The new PM wanted to spend the summer talking about the cost of living – he should change his plans

I don’t think I have ever written before about a British strike directly related to the climate emergency. But that’s exactly what began late last week in north London, with a zeitgeisty connection to Andy Burnham’s fixation on buses: picket lines outside depots and massed walkouts, while the temperatures in the relevant parts of the capital and its suburbs hovered at about 34C (93F).

Last Friday, more than 1,500 drivers employed by the transport giant Arriva began a planned run of 26 stoppages through to October, affecting bus routes spread between London and Essex. items.summary_raw: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces Commander Robert Brovdi allegedly emailed the brother of a Turkish sailor killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on the cargo ship MV Reyhan Sarı near Novorossiysk in July.  The message reportedly stated:   Your brother consciously chose this path. What they did contributed to enriching the Russian Federation, and he got what he deserved.  Savaş Çakar, a Turkish crew member, was killed when the coal-carrying vessel was hit.   His brother Abbas Çakar, a journalist, said the message doubled his anger and vowed to pursue accountability.  Ukraine has not officially confirmed or denied the email.   The family is reportedly preparing an ICC complaint.

items.title: Sky News found that more than 1,300 Strava users shared workout data from US military bases across the Middle East, revealing routes, routines, troop movements and even activity at…
items.summary_raw: Sky News found that more than 1,300 Strava users shared workout data from US military bases across the Middle East, revealing routes, routines, troop movements and even activity at bases not shown on public maps. Many users posted under their real names, potentially making individual personnel identifiable.  Security experts say Iran could have used this information alongside other intelligence to monitor US forces and identify targets.   Sky News highlighted cases in Bahrain and Jordan where changes in Strava activity appeared to reveal where personnel had relocated before locations were later attacked by Iran.  The issue is not new: the Pentagon warned in 2018 that fitness-app location data could endanger troops.   Despite restrictions, personnel from the US and UK have continued sharing activities from sensitive sites, including RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. Sky News also found Strava activity inside Israel’s Dimona nuclear research centre.  Source: Sky News

items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇺🇸⚓️ The U.S. Navy is studying a potentially multibillion-dollar redesign of future Ford-class aircraft carriers after President Donald Trump pushed for ships that look more like the iconic American carriers of the World War II era. According to The Washington Post, one option under review would fundamentally alter the appearance and flight-deck configuration of America’s newest carrier class.  Naval planners are examining whether the carrier’s command tower, known as the “island,” could be moved forward from its current aft position toward the center of the ship. The existing placement was deliberately chosen to improve flight-deck efficiency and safety, creating more space around the catapults, accelerating aircraft launches and reducing turbulence during landings. The Trump administration has also ordered the Navy to develop options for replacing the Ford class’s modern electromagnetic aircraft launch system with traditional steam catapults, emphasizing what it describes as proven, reliable and affordable technology. items.title: Opinion: How Iran and Ukraine are strategically sinking their rivals at sea
items.summary_raw:
Opinion: How Iran and Ukraine are strategically sinking their rivals at sea

The Iran war may be fought primarily remotely via the air, but its strategic outcome is increasingly being decided at sea. 

The latest strikes and counterstrikes have clarified rather than altered that central fact. Washington may escalate through a ground intervention, wider attacks on Iran’s critical infrastructure, or a strike against the deeply buried nuclear-linked complex at Pickaxe Mountain in Isfahan province.

Each option could inflict further damage and expand the war. None, however, is likely to eliminate Iran’s distributed maritime architecture or make the Strait of Hormuz strategically irrelevant.

According to Yonhap, Lee has proposed talks with Pyongyang aimed at formally ending the Korean War, while also calling for practical discussions on halting further development of North Korea’s nuclear program. Lee says his goal is to replace this “unstable armistice system” with a permanent peace framework on the Korean Peninsula. North Korea today possesses a far stronger nuclear arsenal and has dramatically deepened its military partnership with Russia, giving Kim Jong Un considerably less incentive to compromise than during previous rounds of inter-Korean diplomacy. The UK’s biggest gigafactory has shelved plans to expand production in Sunderland because of stalled talks on a deal to supply electric car batteries to Jaguar Land Rover.

Chinese-owned AESC produces batteries for Nissan at its gigafactory next door to the Japanese carmaker’s Sunderland plant. US President Donald Trump has urged Americans to accept slightly higher gasoline prices as the cost of preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

The comments underscore the growing political risk for Trump as higher fuel prices collide with his campaign promise to lower energy costs, with Democrats already seeking to make the economic fallout from the Iran war an issue heading into the November midterm elections.

In a speech in Garden City, Trump said Americans who had to "pay a tiny little bit more for your gasoline" should remember that this was the cost of ensuring "a very evil country" could not have a nuclear weapon.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender RT @sentdefender: An Italian Eurofighter assigned to NATO’s Baltic Air Policing mission shot down a drone of unconfirmed, but likely Russian origin after it entered Latvian airspace Friday, according to NATO and Latvian authorities.  Two Italian Eurofighters scrambled from Lithuania along with two Turkish F-16s from Estonia. One of the Italian jets identified and engaged the drone.  Latvian forces are now searching for the wreckage near Rugāji, about 35 km from the Russian border, so the drone’s origin has not yet been established.  The incident comes amid a growing number of drone incursions into Baltic airspace. Latvia says Ukrainian drones have entered the region several times this year, while officials also point to Russian electronic warfare as a possible factor causing Ukrainian systems to stray across borders.  Before Friday's incident, Ukrainian forces had launched attacks against Russian ports near St. Petersburg. Russian authorities claimed to have intercepted 15 Ukrainian drones during those attacks. items.title: Strong Firefighting Forces on Alert in Halkidiki but Wildfire Situation Has Improved
items.summary_raw:
HALKIDIKI – The wildfire situation in Siviri, Halkidiki, has improved. According to an update from the Fire Service, there is currently no active fire front, although numerous scattered hotspots remain. A total of 227 firefighters, 57 vehicles, 13 foot teams, six firefighting aircraft and one helicopter are operating in the area. All forces operating in Siviri, Kassandra, where the fire broke out the afternoon of Thursday, August 13, remain on alert and at full readiness. The situation Friday morning was significantly improved, and continuous water drops are being carried out to extinguish the remaining small pockets of fire. All forces are maintaining heightened readiness ahead of the significant strengthening of winds expected from midday.

President Donald Trump dismissed concerns Friday over living conditions and the mental health of service members on a US aircraft carrier deployed against Iran and said the ship would soon rotate out.

Asked by reporters whether family members were worried about the situation on the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, Trump said: "No, they're not."

Trump also rejected that the ship - now in its ninth month at sea - had been deployed for too long. "No, no, no, not nearly enough," he said.

Move to dilute ZEV mandate from 80% down to as little as 50% could add millions of tonnes of CO2 to emissions and comes amid record UK heatwaves

Andy Burnham’s government has said it will look at cutting electric vehicle sales targets, in proposals that could add millions of tonnes a year to the UK’s future carbon dioxide emissions.

The government launched a consultation on Friday on cutting the target for new EVs to as little as 50% of all new cars in 2030, down from 80% under existing rules. The consultation will include several options, including leaving the headline target unchanged, or cutting it to 70%, 60% or 50%.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender An Italian Eurofighter assigned to NATO’s Baltic Air Policing mission shot down a drone of unconfirmed, but likely Russian origin after it entered Latvian airspace Friday, according to NATO and Latvian authorities.  Two Italian Eurofighters scrambled from Lithuania along with two Turkish F-16s from Estonia. One of the Italian jets identified and engaged the drone.  Latvian forces are now searching for the wreckage near Rugāji, about 35 km from the Russian border, so the drone’s origin has not yet been established.  The incident comes amid a growing number of drone incursions into Baltic airspace. Latvia says Ukrainian drones have entered the region several times this year, while officials also point to Russian electronic warfare as a possible factor causing Ukrainian systems to stray across borders.  Before Friday's incident, Ukrainian forces had launched attacks against Russian ports near St. Petersburg. Russian authorities claimed to have intercepted 15 Ukrainian drones during those attacks. items.summary_raw:
JD Vance says low energy prices for Americans top priority amid US war on Iran

US Vice President JD Vance said that keeping oil and gas prices low for Americans is now Washington's top priority in its war on Iran. 

"I know that oil is down today and it's way down from the highs in the early days of the conflict," has said on Fox News. "That's goal number one -- keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country."

He added that the next primacy focus for the US is to "ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon".

"When Pete Hegseth was nominated, everyone knew he was completely incompetent," he wrote on X. "Now our brave sailors are paying the price in a horrific and unfathomable way."

"Pete Hegseth must be fired immediately."

items.title: ‘Unprecedented’ rain kills four in Japan as thousands stranded at airport
items.summary_raw:
Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 as torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture as flooding risks remain high despite rainfall easing

At least four people died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport, and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings.

The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people in Chiba and other areas, and about 45,000 homes lost power, as 115mm of rain fell hourly, approximately the same amount usually recorded for the whole month of August.

items.title: Fossils show huge carbon emissions harm forests, not ‘green the planet’
items.summary_raw:
Study of 56m-year-old leaves counters claims from Trump administration members of ‘benefits’ of fossil fuel pollution

Adding huge quantities of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere is set to cause the Earth’s forests to wither and die rather than flourish, according to a new study that counters erroneous claims that fossil fuel pollution will green the planet.

An analysis of fossilized leaf cells from a period known as the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (or PETM), which occurred about 56m years ago, has helped reconstruct how the world’s forests responded when planet-heating gases were previously being released at a rapid rate.

items.title: Britain's scorched fields mean a food crisis – and the government is ignoring the one measure that would help | George Monbiot
items.summary_raw:
This summer’s extreme weather and wars in Iran and Ukraine have made our need for food stockpiles more pressing than ever

When a business makes long-term plans, they call it prudence. When a government makes long-term plans, they call it communism. Any sustained state intervention attracts the prefix “Soviet-style”, and triggers vicious attacks across the billionaire media. So governments have developed a bias against long-term thinking. This may explain why we no longer maintain strategic food reserves.

In Britain, where soils have parched, market analysts warn that we’re facing the most severe food security crisis in decades. Enough new coalmining projects were proposed last year to increase global supplies by 2.5bn tonnes a year, an increase of 11% from the year before, even as demand for coal plateaus, according to a new report.

Global Energy Monitor, an NGO, found that India ignited a rise in new coalmine proposals in 2025 despite a global slowdown in the number of mine openings because of falling demand for the fossil fuel.

items.title: Israel seeking to 'remove Palestine from world's agenda', Erdogan says
items.summary_raw:
Israel seeking to 'remove Palestine from world's agenda', Erdogan says

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Wednesday accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's government of seeking to "remove Palestine" from the world's agenda. 

"The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region," Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart Mahmoud Abbas in Ankara. 

"No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people's hearts as they try to destroy it," he said, vowing Turkey would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

items.title: Erdogan eyes expansion of regional defence pact
items.summary_raw:
Erdogan eyes expansion of regional defence pact

President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has said he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday.

"Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries," the Turkish leader told Asharq Al-Awsat. "Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella." 

Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkey expected Egypt to join the pact "in the next stage", telling the Anadolu state news agency only "a few technical issues" stood in the way. 

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thu

Powerful storms swept across ⁠the midwest on Tuesday, leaving three dead and more than 800,000 without power in four states as winds gusts of more than 80mph (130km/h) tore down trees and power lines.

⁠In Indiana, a four-year-old child died after a tree fell on his ⁠home in Geneva Township and a person died in a suspected weather-related house explosion in Portage, a city about 30 miles south-east of Chicago.

items.title: Heat, algae and AI: proposed datacenter could damage Everglades, experts warn
items.summary_raw:
Plans for hyperscale datacenter in Palm Beach county prompt concerns over water and electricity demands

About 16 miles (26km) south-west of Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Largo estate, near the northern edge of the Florida Everglades, developers have proposed a hyperscale datacenter on a 202-acre (82-hectare) parcel of land surrounded by water. Local environmentalists warn that the proposed 600MW datacenter in western Palm Beach county could damage the wetlands, which the federal government and the state of Florida have spent a combined $6bn to restore after decades of drainage and development.

One concern is that the datacenter could exacerbate an existing issue of toxic bacterial blooms in a water system which has already been stressed by drought, fertilizer runoff and warm water temperatures. In recent summers, the bright blooms of blue-green algae have covered nearly half of Lake Okeechobee, which feeds into the Everglades.

items.title: I was enjoying growing vegetables. Then the climate crisis raised its ugly head | Bim Adewunmi
items.summary_raw:
My child and I were bonding over our hit-and-miss approach to reaping crops. But with heatwaves pushing more of Britain into drought, it’s starting to feel like a luxury we can’t afford

For the first time in my life, I live in a home that has real outdoor space. What a concept! There are no downsides to a garden. Back in spring, I made grand plans – I watched all the TikToks, I bought seeds and trays and pots and grow bags, I ordered soil, a trowel and a watering can. I knew what I was after: super-tiny-scale subsistence farming with a side of Zen. A little fruit, a little veg, lots of flowers to attract pollinators. And I knew I wanted my elder child to gain an understanding of how things come to be and how to cope if and when they fail.

We love a tomato side salad, so that was the first thing we attempted. The seedlings flourished and then died in the first heatwave of the season. An omen, surely. The dahlias, ranunculus and freesias refused to grow, let alone bloom. My enthusiasm began to wane.

The prime minister will chair a meeting of the Cobra emergency committee on Wednesday in response to extreme heat, which has caused wildfires and plunged many parts of Britain into drought.

Andy Burnham will meet with ministers, officials and agencies as high temperatures continue across the UK on Wednesday afternoon, with temperatures of 33C forecast, and up to 38C on Thursday.

items.title: Libya power company says attack on Zawiya caused major outage
items.summary_raw:
Libya power company says attack on Zawiya caused major outage

Libya's General Electricity Company said that an attack on the South Zawiya substation caused a complete wide-scale outage and loss of power supply to a number of areas in the south of Zawiya. 

The company added that repeated targeting have lead to severe damage to the Zawiya power station, and has forced it to withdraw its technical teams.

It warned that the attacks may cause more delays in maintenance and restoration of electricity services.

The Romanian Naval Component Command contacted Ukraine, which confirmed that the aircraft did not belong to Ukrainian forces.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender Iran is adapting its tactics to wear down U.S. air defenses, and exploit dwindling interceptor stocks, according to new reporting from The New York Times.  During five days of attacks on U.S. bases in Jordan last month, Iran combined drones with maneuvering ballistic missiles to overwhelm defensive systems. On July 17, one missile penetrated the defenses at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, killing 3 U.S. soldiers and wounding more than 100.  The scale of the expenditure is becoming increasingly important: the U.S. has fired more than 1,500 Patriot interceptors during the war and reportedly has fewer than 1,700 remaining, while producing only about 600 Patriots in all of 2025. On one day during the Jordan attacks, U.S. forces reportedly fired around 50 Patriots, at roughly $4 million each.  Iran has also demonstrated other adaptations, including using drones to provide targeting data that helped shoot down a U.S. F-15E in April and expanding attacks through partners such as the Houthis to force U.S. forces to defend against threats from multiple directions.  The Pentagon continues to publicly deny that the U.S. has a munitions shortage. tweet

items.title: The Guardian view on wildfires: firefighters can’t handle this crisis alone | Editorial
items.summary_raw:
The response to this summer’s record heat and drought should be led by ministers – not left to the emergency services

The wildfire that began on protected heathland in the New Forest in Hampshire on Sunday was reported to be under control on Tuesday. But with temperatures forecast to reach 36C or higher in parts of England on Thursday, the risk of further outbreaks remains high. Firefighters responded to 185 wildfires in the first 10 days of August. In coastal Suffolk, conservationists and locals are counting the cost of the blaze that devastated Dunwich Heath. Its vegetation and rare bird populations are expected to take decades to recover.

Although the immediate cause of many wildfires is litter, the risks are elevated by heat and drought, and repeated warnings from climate scientists do not necessarily lessen the shock and distress caused. items.title: Three killed in Houthi attack on cargo ship in Bab al-Mandab
items.summary_raw:
Three killed in Houthi attack on cargo ship in Bab al-Mandab

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO), the international reference point for maritime security incidents, has received a report of an attack on a cargo ship in Bab al-Mandab off the coast of Mocha from an "unknown projectile" which resulted "in casualties".

Yemeni official sources from the coast guard and military say at least three crew members have been killed. They say the attack came from the Houthis, which control much of Yemen's Red Sea coast.

Until now, Yemen's Houthis had only targeted tankers carrying Saudi oil in the Bab al-Mandab, not container ships.

It doesn’t have to be this way. We know what needs to be done

Disturbing news about our water resources is now constant and unrelenting. In just the past few weeks, media have reported that Puerto Rico is suffering a deep water crisis as severe drought has cut water supplies to thousands. The Rhine and Po rivers in Europe are at record low levels. The seven states sharing the Colorado River in the US are fighting over unprecedented shortages, while its major reservoirs have shrunk to their lowest levels since they were built.

Hungary’s only nuclear power plant is on the verge of shutting down because there isn’t enough water in the Danube River to cool it. Toxic chemicals have been found

items.title: ‘Extreme heat’ warning issued for parts of England on Thursday as temperatures could reach 38C – latest news
items.summary_raw:
Met Office says this warning will likely cause ‘adverse’ health effects with travel and power generation also possibly affected

The Guardian’s environment editor, Fiona Harvey, has written a useful explainer about the UK public services that are struggling in the extreme weather. You can read it in full here:

There’s only one solution in the end to the drought now declared across most of England and that’s rain, says Hannah Cloke, professor of hydrology at the University of Reading.

An important consequence of drought is that very dry soils can become less able to absorb rainfall when it does arrive. This can increase surface runoff and can even contribute to localised flash flooding, particularly if rain falls intensely over a short period.

The current situation highlights the need to improve long-term resilience to both drought and flood risk as climate variability increases, and shows one more damaging impact of the burning of fossil fuels.

American officials said security personnel transferred him inside a catering container to a military plane over a threat from Iran against him and Air Force One.  Publicly, Trump and other officials said he would leave Turkey on July 8 aboard one of the older versions of Air Force One, rather than the luxury Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar that he arrived in. Trump told reporters he was switching planes "in memory of the good old days."  He boarded the older plane through the door on its left side, in full view of the cameras. Media outlets reported he flew it to Britain, where he transferred back to the newer plane. The Times had reported at the time that the decision was partly due to safety concerns over the Qatari-donated jet, which did not have all the security features installed on the older versions.  But instead of taking off on the old 747, Trump was secretly removed from it inside a catering container hoisted to the opposite side of the plane, away from where the journalists who flew with him boarded. items.title: Iran to increase gas production, says state minister
items.summary_raw:
Iran to increase gas production, says state minister

Iran will bring back 95 million cubic metres of gas to its production cycle by the end of September, oil minister Mohsen Paknejad said on Tuesday, according to the oil ministry's news outlet, as Tehran conducts repairs on energy infrastructure targeted by Israel and the US.

In July, a senior government official said Iran expects to restore around 100 million cubic metres per day of natural gas production capacity "within the coming months", after air strikes removed about 230 million cubic metres from output since the war started on 28 February.

items.title: Tuesday briefing: To drill or not to drill – Burnham’s first big climate test
items.summary_raw:
In today’s newsletter: As we enter our fifth summer heatwave, Andy Burnham’s government is looking at what the UK should do with its remaining North Sea oil and gas

Good morning. What a difference a new job can make. “To have a shot at staying within 1.5C global warming, we can’t have any new oil or gasfields … It’s irresponsible and shortsighted to be funding new #fossilfuels when we need to be getting to #NetZero.”

This was the 2022 message from Miatta Fahnbulleh, now the secretary of state for energy security and net zero. It’s a testament to her remarkable rise that Fahnbulleh wasn’t even an MP when she posted it four years ago. Today, she is in the cabinet, facing (or is the face of, at least) one of the most challenging, and potentially controversial questions looming for the new government: to drill or not to drill, baby?

Two sites are the focus of fierce debate. Yesterday, a public consultation on whether to greenlight extraction at one of them – Jackdaw – closed. Next Monday, it’ll be the same for the other, Rosebank. Andy Burnham

items.summary_raw:
Libyan intelligence chief for Haftar's eastern-based forces assassinated: Report

The head of the military intelligence department for Libya's eastern-based forces led by Khalifa Haftar was killed in a targeted assassination on Monday, Anadolu Agency reported citing a Libyan security official.

An explosive device planted under Fawzi al-Mansouri's vehicle exploded in al-Sayyida Aisha residential neighborhood in eastern Benghazi.

According to the report, the official described the incident as a "terrorist attack," however, no official statement has been issued so far on the assassination.

Based on the latest Fire Service update, the situation regarding the wildfire that started in Kouvaras on Monday morning was considerably improved, with strong firefighting forces now only dealing with numerous still-smoking spots within its perimeter. Earlier, the advancing flames had ruined installations at a poultry-farming unit near the village of Agios Stylianos.

The technology is considered so advanced and highly classified that the White House reportedly restricts its export even to some of America's closest allies.  The reversal represents a significant setback for Kyiv's efforts to establish greater domestic production capacity for Patriot-related systems and reduce its dependence on limited deliveries of U.S.-made interceptors.  For Ukraine, the challenge now becomes finding a production model that can expand its Patriot capabilities while satisfying Washington's strict technology-security requirements. items.title: UAE oil company announces new investments to bypass Hormuz
items.summary_raw:
UAE oil company announces new investments to bypass Hormuz

Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (Adnoc), the Emirate's national oil company, announced plans to construct a new gas export facility to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The company reported its income for the second quarter of 2026 earlier today, beating forecasts with a net income of $665m and strong guidance for the rest of the year, contingent on exports being fully restored in the fourth quarter.

Adnoc also announced its intention to construct a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility on the eastern coast of the UAE, which would allow it to move LNG out of the Persian Gulf without having to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

The company's ships have come under repeated attacks while transiting through Hormuz, with three of its vessels having been attacked

items.title: Western Europe Sets New Temperature Record as Heat Waves, Drought and Wildfires Pummel the Region
items.summary_raw: PARIS (AP) — Europe is enduring another exceptionally hot summer, with persistent heat waves fueling wildfires, prolonged drought and new temperature records across the continent, while Western Europe has set a new average temperature record for the June-July period. The average temperature in Western Europe for June and July reached 21.62 C (70.92 F), according to the European climate agency Copernicus, surpassing the previous record set in 2022. The extreme heat has affected countries across Europe since May, with France, in particular, facing repeated heat waves and record-breaking temperatures. The latest episode is expected to bring temperatures approaching 40 C (104 F) in southeastern France from Tuesday onward, as the country braces for its fifth heat wave alert of the season. “Persistent high-pressure systems trapped heat over western Europe, the extreme temperatures also amplified widespread drought. In the west, Ukrainian forces cleared the southern dachas of Prymorske from earlier Russian infiltrations and expanded their foothold south of the Sukhyy River in northern Plavni. From there, they pushed further south, improving their positions in the central part of Plavni, where Russia is now dropping KAB glide-bombs. Other assault groups advanced further down the highway and are attempting to reach the northern outskirts of Kamyanske.  To the northeast, the Ukrainians finally cleared the remaining part of Stepnohirsk north of the Sukhyy River after multiple months of intense fighting, before subsequently establishing control over Aharna Street south of the river. From here, they are attempting to enter the southernmost high-rise micro-district of the town. items.title: Typhoon Dolphin: more than a million people evacuated in China as record rainfall dumped on Shanghai
items.summary_raw:
Authorities warn that days of intense rain could trigger widespread flooding and landslides as storm moves north and further inland

More than a million people were moved to safety across eastern China by Sunday evening as powerful Typhoon Dolphin made landfall amid fears torrential rain would cause flooding and landslides.

Wenzhou, a coastal city in Zhejiang province, said it relocated more than 900,000 people and opened more than 1,500 emergency shelters. In neighbouring Fujian, 98,900 people were moved from high-risk areas.

items.title: World’s seas have hit hottest temperature on record for July, say scientists
items.summary_raw:
Average sea surface temperature outside polar regions was highest on record for July, beating previous high in 2023

The world’s seas were hotter last month than in any July on record, scientists have said, as devastating heat struck western Europe.

Sea surface temperatures hit record highs for July on the Atlantic coast and western Mediterranean, the EU’s Copernicus climate change service found, with severe marine heatwaves roiling Europe’s seas. Globally, the average sea surface temperature outside the cold polar regions was the highest on record for the month, beating the previous July record set in 2023.

items.title: ELINT News RT @bayraktar_1love: Satellite imagery of the "anti-Starlink" Volna Kupol Garant electronic-warfare complex which was destroyed in Gelendzhik today.  What makes this str…
items.summary_raw: ELINT News RT @bayraktar_1love: Satellite imagery of the "anti-Starlink" Volna Kupol Garant electronic-warfare complex which was destroyed in Gelendzhik today.  What makes this strike interesting is the location. Similar complexes have previously been destroyed on occupied Ukrainian territory, but this one was deployed on Russia’s mainland, on the Black Sea coast.  The Ukrainian Defense Forces destroyed a Russian Volna Kupol Garant electronic warfare (EW) system in Gelendzhik, as evidenced by satellite imagery of military unit No. 2156 dated August 7.  The Volna Kupol Garant is a Russian EW system designed to disrupt Starlink satellite communications. The system generates directed radio interference toward the satellite, preventing it from receiving signals from ground-based Starlink terminals.  This is already the third destruction of this system documented in open sources.  Coordinates: 44.571383° 37.989556° - Dnipro Osint tweet
